subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class non-thread persistent `sessions_spawn` contract for native and ACP child sessions, and what routing/lifecycle owner should handle follow-up delivery?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the requested behavior changes session ownership, child output delivery, cleanup, and channel binding semantics across native subagents and ACP harnesses, which is a product/runtime contract choice rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Define the contract first
options.body: Approve a generic non-thread persistent-session design covering session creation, `sessions_send` targeting, parent-delivery behavior, cleanup, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Keep session mode thread-bound
options.body: Keep `mode="session"` as a thread-bound concept and direct users to `mode="run"`, `/acp --bind here`, or narrower affinity work for unthreaded cases.

options.title: Split ACP and native work
options.body: Handle ACP persistent affinity through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55484 while leaving native subagent non-thread persistence for a separate design.

recommendation.title: Define the contract first
recommendation.body: Approve a generic non-thread persistent-session design covering session creation, `sessions_send` targeting, parent-delivery behavior, cleanup, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting product/runtime boundary decision, and steipete is listed as project owner with recent core thread-binding refactor history.
